transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-05-20 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 55 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lyra VP Eng), Liam O'Neal (Lyra SRE), Priya Rao (Lyra Security)

Summary: Quick sync to walk through postmortem findings from the 2026-05-18 outage, confirm mitigations, and agree next steps for reliability improvements and security review.

Topics: incident timeline, root cause (KV cache degradation + autoscaler), immediate mitigations, longer-term reliability fixes (autoscaler tuning, prefix caching), security requests (KMS/HSM, audit logs), benchmarking plan.

Action items (recap at end too): see metadata action_items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time right after the weekend. we'll keep this tight, 45, 50 minutes ish.
[00:20] Maya (Lyra VP Eng): thanks Sofia. yeah, big thanks to the team for the postmortem doc. we wanted to walk through the RCA and make sure we align on mitigations and their timeline.
[01:15] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick recap from our side: on 05-18 we saw a spike in tail latency caused by the KV cache (initially mitigated locally) but then the autoscaler misfired due to the burst pattern and provisioned nodes too slowly so queues built up. the quantized runtime patch we rolled helped reduce per-token time but the root was the cache eviction pattern.
[03:10] Liam (Lyra SRE): yeah, we saw the queues back up. our logs show lots of retries, and then the VPC flapping was a factor — sometimes the nodes couldn't reach the K-V cash store (the transcription notes it as K-V cash).
[05:30] Priya (Lyra Security): from security side we flagged that during the incident we couldn't correlate a couple of request traces to user IDs because some of the audit logs weren't forwarded to Splunk due to a drain failure. we also need confirmation on the KMS integration and key rotation schedule.
[07:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): understood. on the KMS point, Redwood's private deployments support both KMS and HSM and we can share the integration doc; we'll also include our SOC 2 attestation and the encryption flow.
[08:45] Maya: great. can you also share the list of SDK / runtime versions that were running during the incident? our config management needs that to reproduce.
[09:20] Ethan: yes, we'll include the exact runtime build: rdx-infer v1.8.3+quant-patch-2 and the autoscaler ruleset we had — note there was a custom cooldown set to 180s which delayed scale-up.
[11:40] Liam: that cooldown is tricky; we had hoped to keep cost down but in this case it hurt latency. question: what are the tradeoffs if we reduce cooldown to 60s? cost vs latency?
[12:10] Ethan: reducing cooldown to 60s will improve tail latency significantly for bursty workloads, but you pay slightly higher cost during spikes. we discussed smarter scaling policies — for example policy that uses queue depth and p99 latency as triggers, not just CPU.
[15:00] Maya: is there a built-in policy we can use or do we have to script it?
[15:30] Ethan: Redwood has a template we can enable — we'll send the policy JSON. also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for hot prompts; that helped in our internal stress tests.
[18:20] Priya: on audit / compliance, we need to know retention windows for trace logs and whether we can push to our SIEM. also SOAP or SAML SSO logs for user sessions.
[19:05] Sofia: yes, SIEM forwarding is supported; we'll send the steps for Splunk/Datadog forwarding. SSO is SAML and we log session assertions; these are in the security pack.
[20:02] Maya: can we also get an action plan for a canary to validate the autoscaler changes before we apply to prod? we want to avoid another incident mid-day.
[22:00] Ethan: propose this plan: 1) run perf bench with current runtime and quant patch on a dedicated dev cluster, 2) apply reduced cooldown + queue-depth trigger in canary region for 48 hours, 3) monitor p95/p99 and rollback if regressions. Ethan will own the bench run.
[25:40] Liam: for bench details, can you include batch sizes and sequence lengths? our prod mix has variable lengths and small batch sizes.
[26:10] Ethan: sure — we'll run seq length distribution matching your traces: median 128, p95 512, batch profiles: [1,2,4,8]. I'll include configs.
[28:00] Priya: on security validation, we need Redwood to confirm no sensitive payloads are cached in plaintext if prefix caching is enabled. does Redwood mask user PII in logs?
[29:10] Sofia: we don't store PII in logs by default; log redaction can be configured and prefix caching is configurable to avoid storing full user prompts. we'll include the redaction and data handling doc.
[32:30] Maya: timeline wise, when can we get the initial bench outputs?
[33:00] Ethan: aiming for 5 business days — so by 2026-05-27. I'll upload CSV and a short notes doc.
[35:45] Liam: aside from autoscaler config, what longer-term reliability improvements are recommended?
[36:10] Ethan: items: autoscaler policy changes, more aggressive prefix caching for hot routes, add a small standby buffer (reserved capacity) for critical endpoints, and better alerting on queue depth. these reduce unit cost benefits a bit but improve SLOs.
[39:05] Maya: reserved capacity — that ties to Redwood Dedicated? what's the minimum commitment?
[39:30] Sofia: we can run you a short cost model: reserved capacity vs burst on hosted. depends on throughput. we'll share a cost/latency tradeoff spreadsheet.
[42:30] Priya: also need the SOC 2 cert and any pen test results we can share with our audit team.
[43:00] Sofia: yes, will attach SOC 2 and summary redaction; full pen test reports we can share under NDA — we'll coordinate with your legal.
[46:10] Maya: any blockers from Redwood to running the canary?
[46:30] Ethan: none technical — just need access to a canary cluster and the permission to change autoscaler rule for that namespace. coordinate with Liam's team.
[48:00] Liam: we can provision canary cluster by Monday and give you RBAC.
[50:10] Sofia: ok, recap next steps: we'll send the postmortem deck (Sofia), Ethan runs bench and posts results (Ethan), Priya will confirm KMS details (Priya), and we'll schedule a remediation planning call for week of 05-25.
[52:05] Maya: thanks everyone. quick note — please include the exact log snippets for the moment of eviction so our engineers can reproduce.
[53:10] Ethan: noted, will include logs and the exact runtime build.
[54:40] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up in email. end.
